chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام was asked about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Glorious:
"But repentance is not for those who keep doing evil deeds until, when death comes to one of them, he says: Indeed, I repent now."
He عليه السلام said: "That is when he directly witnesses the matter of the Hereafter."

key_terms.أَمْرَ الْآخِرَةِ: the reality and affair of the Hereafter becoming manifest
key_terms.التَّوْبَةُ: repentance; returning to Allah after sin
key_terms.السَّيِّئَاتِ: evil deeds or sins committed persistently
key_terms.الْآنَ: now; the final moment when repentance is declared too late
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death; the moment of departure from worldly life
key_terms.عَايَنَ: he directly witnessed or beheld with certainty

ai.seo_question: When is repentance no longer accepted according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the verse refers to repentance made only after the dying person begins to witness the realities of the Hereafter. At that point, repentance is no longer a genuine turning in faith before the unseen, but comes after direct confrontation with the consequences of one's deeds.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.352 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about the words of Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious:
"But repentance is not [accepted] of those who [continue to] do evil deeds up until, when death comes to one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I repent now’." (Surah An Nisa 4:18).
Imam (as) said: "That is when they witness the realities of the Hereafter."
